review_notes: I read the whole file and compared proofs that look alike. I also read both `Package` structures and both `package_range` theorems in finite-etale-algebras. Two repetitions looked substantial. (1) The two reverse-inclusion proofs, `..._of_purelyInseparable` and `..._of_isSepClosure`, are line-for-line identical apart from the descent package and its `package_range`. (2) The two surjectivity proofs, `..._surjective_of_isSepClosed` and `componentBaseChangeComparisonAlgHom_surjective`, share a long setup and finish. I did not report the duplicated local-instance block in the second namespace (lines about 598–1300 re-declare the primed local instances) because it is mostly boilerplate. I also did not report the `ModelIso`/`Iso` pairs that repeat for the special case and the general case, because they are thin wrappers. I cannot run Lean. The shared lemmas below are sketches. The main uncertainty is whether the local `Algebra K (P ⊗[k] K)` instances (`tensorProductRightAlgebra` in the first block, `rightAlgebra` in the second) are defeq, so that the lemma can be used in the second block.

findings.problem: The purely inseparable and separable-closure reverse-inclusion proofs are the same argument, about 50 lines each (lines 204–256 and 987–1043). Both build `pkg.algebra`, show it lies in `componentSubalgebra X`, and form `inclusion` and the `hmap` identity `scalarExtensionMap ∘ map id inclusion = scalarExtensionMap pkg.algebra`. Both then pull `e.symm x` back along the range equation, produce `w` via `commRight`, and finish with the same chain of `change`, `rw [show ... by simp [w]]` and `calc`. The only differences are the descent package (`PurelyInseparableDescent.package P hP` versus `SeparableClosureDescent.package P hstable hP`) and the matching `package_range` rewrite. Any fix to the nontrivial `commRight`/`hmap`/`e.symm` bookkeeping must be made twice, in two places that sit about 780 lines apart.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one private lemma before the purely inseparable case. It takes the descended subalgebra as data and has no hypothesis on the field extension:

`private theorem componentSubalgebra_le_baseChangedComponentSubalgebra_of_range (X : Over (Spec (.of k))) [LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom] [QuasiCompact X.hom] (D : Subalgebra k Γ(X.left, ⊤)) (hD : D.IsFiniteEtale) (hrange : (SeparableClosureDescent.scalarExtensionMap (K := K) D).range = pulledBackComponentSubalgebra (K := K) X) : componentSubalgebra (schemeBaseChange X (L := K)) ≤ baseChangedComponentSubalgebra (K := K) X`.

Proof sketch: move the current body from `have hD : pkg.algebra ≤ ...` to the final `calc` into this lemma, with `pkg.algebra` replaced by `D`, `pkg.isFiniteEtale` by `hD`, and the `rw [package_range ...]` replaced by `rw [hrange]`.

The two uses become short:
- Purely inseparable case (hypotheses `[IsPurelyInseparable k K] [IsSepClosed K]`): `let pkg := PurelyInseparableDescent.package (pulledBackComponentSubalgebra (K := K) X) (pulledBackComponentSubalgebra_isFiniteEtale (K := K) X); exact ..._of_range (K := K) X pkg.algebra pkg.isFiniteEtale (PurelyInseparableDescent.package_range _ _)`.
- Separable-closure case (hypothesis `[IsSepClosure k K]`): the same with `SeparableClosureDescent.package P hstable hP` and `SeparableClosureDescent.package_range P hstable hP`.

The lemma's statement does not mention the tensor-product `Algebra K` instance. The extra `let _ : Algebra K (componentSubalgebra X ⊗[k] K) := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra` in the second use (lines 993–994) should then be unnecessary.
findings.benefit: The `commRight`/`hmap` transport argument appears once. The two descent theorems then say only which descent package supplies `D` and its range equation, which is the real difference between the cases. Later changes to the global-sections or tensor orientation need one edit instead of two.

have hsource : Module.finrank K (P ⊗[k] K) = Module.finrank k P := by
    calc
      Module.finrank K (P ⊗[k] K) = Module.finrank K (K ⊗[k] P) :=

findings.problem: Both surjectivity proofs repeat the same setup and finish. They declare the same `P`, `Q`, `f` and `rightAlgebra` instance, and the same three `Module.Finite` instances. Both prove `hsource : finrank K (P ⊗[k] K) = finrank k P` with the same `commRight`/`finrank_baseChange` calc. Both conclude with an injective linear map between finite-dimensional spaces of equal `finrank`, using `LinearMap.injective_iff_surjective_of_finrank_eq_finrank`, together with `componentBaseChangeComparisonAlgHom_injective`. The `_of_isSepClosed` proof (lines 1141–1174) only proves `finrank K Q ≤ finrank K (P ⊗ K)`. The arbitrary-extension proof (lines 1180–1213) proves `finrank K Q = finrank k P`. Everything else is duplicated.
findings.proposed_change:
Factor out the common conclusion:

`private theorem componentBaseChangeComparisonAlgHom_surjective_of_finrank_le (X : Over (Spec (.of k))) [LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom] [QuasiCompact X.hom] (h : Module.finrank K (componentSubalgebra (schemeBaseChange X (L := K))) ≤ Module.finrank k (componentSubalgebra X)) : Function.Surjective (componentBaseChangeComparisonAlgHom (K := K) X)`.

Proof sketch: set up the `Module.Finite` instances once, prove `hsource` once, get `hge` from `componentBaseChangeComparisonAlgHom_injective` and `LinearMap.finrank_le_finrank_of_injective`, rewrite `h` with `hsource` to get `hle`, and finish with `LinearMap.injective_iff_surjective_of_finrank_eq_finrank`.

The uses are then:
- Separably closed base: `exact ..._of_finrank_le X (by rw [← componentSubalgebra_finrank_eq_natCard_connectedComponents X]; exact componentSubalgebra_baseChange_finrank_le_of_isSepClosed (K := K) X)`.
- Arbitrary extension: `exact ..._of_finrank_le X htarget.le`, where `htarget` is the existing `calc` through `natCard_connectedComponents_separableClosures_eq`.

The lemma needs no new assumptions, since both proofs already use only the quasi-compactness and locally-finite-type instances on `X`.
findings.benefit: Each of the two theorems keeps only the connected-component counting that distinguishes it. The finite-dimensional linear-algebra step and instance setup are written once. A reader can see at once that the whole content is `finrank K Q ≤ finrank k P`.
